title: Headwaters
tagline: Open data sources, described well enough to use from a shell — and probed, so the catalogue knows what still answers.
blurb: Forty open data sources, each one a JSON record with its licence, auth, rate limit, the traps that cost an hour, copy-pasteable recipes, and — the part nobody else keeps — small real requests with stated expectations that a script re-runs to prove the endpoint still works. Building it turned up six live failures nothing else documents: data.gov's CKAN API 404s on every documented path while its API gateway authenticates your key and redirects you to the dead origin; NOAA's GHCN station list and SWPC's solar-wind feed both moved; Jeff Sackmann's tennis_atp and tennis_wta, the basis of most public tennis analytics, are gone; the Census API without a key returns an HTML page with HTTP 200 so the failure reaches you as a JSON parse error; and the GitHub contents API silently caps a directory at 1,000 entries, which hid 199 datasets from this repository's own first harvest. A companion harvester pulls 3,600 candidates from Data Is Plural, TidyTuesday and the AWS open-data registry into a queue to work through.
